key_artists.name: Ken Sugimori
key_artists.why: Collector references pin Ken Sugimori to this Battle Road Summer 2002 No.3 Trainer row, while Bulbapedia's Sugimori page supplies the broader franchise-art context. The credit helps an agent search and compare, but it remains collector-reference-supported until stronger row-level print proof is attached.

claims.text: The local catalog models Battle Road Summer 2002 regional third place prize as one unnumbered promotional source row containing No.3 Trainer at source index 252.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.3 Trainer e-Card Era print was awarded to third-place winners of each regional Battle Road Summer 2002 tournament, held between July and August 2002.

Bulbapedia's Elite Four Trainer page gives the Battle Road Summer 2002 regional schedule as Hokkaido on July 20, Tohoku on July 24, Kanto on July 27-28, Chubu on July 31, Kansai on August 3-4, Chugoku/Shikoku on August 9, and Kyushu on August 11, followed by finals in Tokyo on August 17.
Bulbapedia says the Battle Road 2002 series was the first to introduce the Master age division for players 18 and over, in addition to Junior and Senior divisions.
Bulbapedia says the 2002 No.3 Trainer versions were the last to include the winner's name and regional conference on the card itself and the last to feature male and female variants.
Bulbapedia gives the No.3 Trainer Battle Road Summer 2002 text as recognizing and praising the third-place winner of the Pokémon Card Game Official Tournament.
PokeBoon's exact Battle Road Summer 2002 No.3 Trainer page lists Ken Sugimori as illustrator; this is useful collector-reference support, not primary-source print authority.
PokeBoon's exact Battle Road Summer 2002 No.3 Trainer page lists the distribution date range as July 20 through August 11, 2002.

Pokumon's Battle Road 2002 research reconstructs Summer 2002 No.3 Trainer distribution as 4 girls and 50 boys from Trainers Magazine winner data; this is a collector estimate, not an official copy count.

Pokumon says Summer 2002 winners received a black folio containing the trophy card and certificate, with gold embossing rather than the Spring dark-blue/silver presentation; organizers collected folios after photos and mailed personalized cards back later in September 2002.
Bulbapedia says Battle Road Summer 2002, unlike Spring, culminated in a Best in Japan final with a new card awarded to top ranking players.

Pokumon says Junior league winners of Battle Road Summer 2002 were invited to the International Tropical Mega Battle 2002 in Hawaii, and that the numbered regional Trainer cards from Battle Road Spring and Summer 2002 were the final No.1-No.3 Trainers given away at a regional level before numbered Trainer trophies moved to World Championships.

Bulbapedia's Ken Sugimori page says there are many Pokémon TCG cards illustrated by Sugimori, though most include reused artwork from games, and indexes his broad official artwork role in the franchise.

As judged collector texture, this No.3 Trainer matters because it makes the podium broad enough to see people rather than only victors: venue, rank, name, conference, folio, mail-back, finals context, and variant all remain separate coordinates.

Agents should preserve No.3 rank, Battle Road Summer 2002 regional third-place route, source index 252, July 20-August 11 distribution window, e-Card Era layout, winner name and regional conference fields, male/female variant boundary, black folio/gold-embossing provenance, Summer-vs-Spring distinction, and non-equivalence with Best in Japan photo cards, Elite Four Trainer, No.1/No.2 Trainer, Worlds, Neo Road, or other No.3 Trainer eras before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Battle Road Summer 2002 No.3 Trainer: the wider edge of the podium
narrative.why_it_matters: No.3 Trainer is the card that makes the Summer 2002 podium feel populated. First place is easy to mythologize, second place carries the ache of almost, but third place is where the apparatus shows breadth: dozens of regional players, gendered variants, personalized names, black folios, a September return from the organizers, and a circuit that was already pointing toward national and international stages. It is a trophy card, yes, but more than that it is a map of how many people Pokémon tried to remember.

narrative.human_title: No.3 Trainer, Summer 2002: the card that lets the whole podium breathe
narrative.why_it_matters: This card is the far edge of the regional podium, and that edge matters. It says the circuit cared enough to print a third-place memory with rank, name, region, variant, and mail-back context. For an agent, that is exactly the lesson: do not buy a famous trophy word.
